titulo: Module 03 — Quiz: structured output, validation with retry, and the Batch API

questoes.pergunta: Which current Messages API parameter makes the RESPONSE follow a JSON schema?
opcoes: output_format at the top level of the request, alongside model
response_format
tool_choice: {type: json}
output_config.format with json_schema
questoes.explicacao: Structured outputs use output_config.format; the top-level output_format is deprecated.
feedbacks: Incorrect: deprecated.
Incorrect: that's not the parameter name in the Messages API.
Incorrect: no such tool_choice type exists.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: What requirement must the schema meet in order to use strict: true?
opcoes: Have at least one field of type string
additionalProperties: false on every object
Use only numeric types
Declare minimum and maximum on every numeric field in the schema
questoes.explicacao: Strict requires closed objects (additionalProperties: false). Optional properties are allowed but count toward a limit; the recommendation is required + nullable.
feedbacks: Incorrect: there's no type requirement.
Correct.
Incorrect: any basic type is supported.
Incorrect: numeric ranges aren't even guaranteed by strict.

questoes.pergunta: In extraction via tool use, what is the extracted JSON?
opcoes: The input of the tool_use block the model generates
The content of the tool_result you send back
The free text after the tool_use
The response's usage field
questoes.explicacao: The tool exists only as a schema: the tool_use input is the structured data.
feedbacks: Correct.
Incorrect: tool_result is what you would send back after executing a tool.
Incorrect: free text has no format guarantee.
Incorrect: usage is the token count.

questoes.pergunta: On a newer model, tool_choice: {type: tool, name: extract} returns a 400. Which alternative is recommended if the tool existed only to obtain JSON?
opcoes: tool_choice: {type: any}
An assistant prefill with '{'
Structured outputs via output_config.format
Remove the schema and ask for JSON in the text
questoes.explicacao: On newer models, forced any/tool returns a 400; structured outputs are the substitute when the goal was only JSON.
feedbacks: Incorrect: any is also forced and also returns a 400.
Incorrect: prefill also returns a 400 on newer models.
Correct.
Incorrect: it loses the format guarantee.

questoes.pergunta: The strict schema validates every output, but the sum of the line items doesn't match the total on 3% of the invoices. What does this show?
opcoes: That strict is turned off
That max_tokens needs to be increased
Schema ≠ semantics: validate the sum in code
That the model needs a lower temperature to add up accurately
questoes.explicacao: A schema guarantees type and format; business rules (sums, dates) are validated in your code.
feedbacks: Incorrect: the format is correct; the problem is semantic.
Incorrect: there's no truncation.
Correct.
Incorrect: temperature isn't the problem (and it's rejected on newer models).

questoes.pergunta: The document sometimes has no due date, and the model makes one up. Which schema adjustment helps?
opcoes: Make the due_date field nullable
Remove due_date from required without strict
Add format: date
Add an enum with possible dates
questoes.explicacao: A nullable field gives the model an honest way out (null) instead of forcing it to make something up.
feedbacks: Correct.
Incorrect: without strict you lose the format guarantee, and an optional field doesn't prevent fabrication. Prefer required + nullable.
Incorrect: format guarantees the format; it doesn't prevent fabrication.
Incorrect: it makes no sense for dates.

questoes.pergunta: An expense classification has a closed enum [travel, food, software]. Rental expenses are being classified as 'software'. Which schema pattern solves this?
opcoes: Make the category field a free-form string
Add 'unclear' to the enum
Remove the enum and use few-shot
Add 'other' to the enum plus a detail field
questoes.explicacao: An enum with 'other' + detail avoids forcing a wrong category and preserves the information.
feedbacks: Incorrect: it loses the standardization of the known categories.
Incorrect: 'unclear' is for an ambiguous source; here the category is clear, it's just not on the list.
Incorrect: it loses the structural guarantee.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: When should you use the value 'unclear' in an enum?
opcoes: When the category exists but isn't on the list
When the source is ambiguous or illegible
When the field is numeric
Always, as a default value
questoes.explicacao: 'unclear' avoids guessing when the source doesn't allow a decision.
feedbacks: Incorrect: that case calls for 'other' + detail.
Correct.
Incorrect: it's an enum of categories, not numbers.
Incorrect: making it the default would hide decidable cases.

questoes.pergunta: Which of these constraints does strict mode NOT support, so it must be validated in your code?
opcoes: minimum: 0 on a numeric field
An enum of allowed values
additionalProperties: false
string vs. number type
questoes.explicacao: Numeric ranges (as well as string length, arrays beyond minItems 0/1, and recursion) aren't supported: in a raw schema they return a 400; the SDK helpers move them into the description and validate locally.
feedbacks: Correct.
Incorrect: enum is supported.
Incorrect: it is required and supported.
Incorrect: basic types are guaranteed.

questoes.pergunta: Which retry message is the most effective in a validation loop?
opcoes: 'The JSON is invalid. Try again.'
'Review your answer more carefully and check every field before responding.'
'Error 422.'
'total 1250.00 ≠ sum of items 1205.00 (item 3?)'
questoes.explicacao: Specific errors (what and where) give the model something to fix.
feedbacks: Incorrect: generic; it tends to produce the same response.
Incorrect: vague.
Incorrect: a code with no context (the generic-error anti-pattern).
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: The service recipient's CNPJ field still comes back wrong after 3 retries, and the document doesn't contain the CNPJ. What should you do?
opcoes: Raise the limit to 10 retries
Change the prompt to 'find the CNPJ at all costs'
null in the field + human review, if the business requires it
Fill it in with the service provider's CNPJ
questoes.explicacao: Retry doesn't recover information that is missing from the source; insisting only leads to fabrication.
feedbacks: Incorrect: more attempts, same missing data.
Incorrect: it induces hallucination.
Correct.
Incorrect: fabricated/wrong data.

questoes.pergunta: Why extract both the stated total and the calculated sum of the line items?
opcoes: To save tokens
To detect discrepancies instead of hiding them
Because strict requires duplicate fields to validate numbers
So the Batch API can match the results
questoes.explicacao: Stated + calculated exposes inconsistencies in the document or in the extraction.
feedbacks: Incorrect: it costs a bit more, not less.
Correct.
Incorrect: there's no such requirement.
Incorrect: the batch matches by custom_id.

questoes.pergunta: Which statement about the Batch API is correct?
opcoes: It guarantees a response within 1 hour
It returns results in the same order as the requests
It supports a multi-turn tool loop within a request
~50% cheaper, up to 24h, no SLA
questoes.explicacao: 50% discount, up to 24h, no SLA; results come back out of order; no multi-turn tool use.
feedbacks: Incorrect: there's no SLA; it can take up to 24h.
Incorrect: out of order → match by custom_id.
Incorrect: each request is a single call.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: Which use of the Batch API is APPROPRIATE?
opcoes: Overnight analysis of the day's 200,000 tickets
A mandatory check before merging a PR
Responding to the customer in the support chat
Interactive debugging of a prompt
questoes.explicacao: Batch is for volume with nobody waiting.
feedbacks: Correct.
Incorrect: a blocking step; the PR could wait up to 24h.
Incorrect: real time.
Incorrect: interactive work requires a fast response.

questoes.pergunta: A batch of 10,000 requests has finished: 9,700 succeeded, 250 errored, and 50 expired. Which TWO actions are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Resubmit the entire batch to ensure consistency
Match each result to its source document by custom_id
Resubmit only the custom_ids that errored or expired
Match the results by the order of the lines in the input file
Discard the failed ones, since 97% is a good rate
questoes.explicacao: Results come back out of order (match by custom_id), and only the failed ones are resubmitted.
feedbacks: Incorrect: it wastes money reprocessing 9,700 successes.
Correct.
Correct.
Incorrect: results arrive out of order.
Incorrect: silently discarding means losing data (error suppression).
